hints: Focus on the strict test for chirality, a carbon with four single bonds to four completely different groups.
Look at the long side chain first, every carbon there is part of a C=C double bond or bonded to OH, so none can be sp3 with four single bonds.
Now check the six-membered ring carbon by carbon and see if any sp3 carbon really has four different groups attached.
walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as chiral**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four single bonds to four different atoms or groups. No double bonds allowed at that carbon.

Rule to apply:
$$\text{chiral C} = \text{C with 4 single bonds + 4 different groups}$$

**Rule out the whole side chain**

Look at the long chain to the right. Every carbon is part of a $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond, except the final $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ carbon.

That $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ carbon has two H atoms, so it has two identical groups and cannot be chiral. So the chain gives zero.

**Check the six-membered ring**

The ring has two $\text{C}=\text{C}$ carbons, so they cannot be chiral. The other four ring carbons are $\text{sp}^3$ $\text{CH}_2$ or $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ groups.

The top carbon has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups. Each $\text{CH}_2$ carbon has two identical H atoms. So none has four different groups.

**Count and conclude**

No carbon in the chain and no carbon in the ring passes the four different single-bond test.

Therefore:
$$\text{number of chiral centres} = 0$$

options.A: Correct. Every double-bonded C is planar sp2 and cannot be chiral. Every sp3 C either has two H atoms (CH2 groups) or two CH3 groups, so none has four different groups. Total is 0.
options.B: Incorrect. Students often pick the quaternary ring carbon with the two CH3 groups, thinking branching means chirality. It has two identical methyl groups, so it fails the four different groups test.
options.C: Incorrect. Students sometimes count alkene carbons with two different-looking sides as chiral centres. Alkene C atoms have only three groups and a double bond, so they can show E/Z isomerism but never chirality.
options.D: Incorrect. This comes from counting several sp3 CH2 groups in the ring as chiral just because they are in a ring. A CH2 always has two identical H atoms, so it can never be a chiral centre.
